query: For CrFeCoNiX high-entropy alloys (X = Si, Mn, or Al) in a single- or multiphase metallic solid-solution state, what single testable mechanistic hypothesis could explain whether a stable, coherent, slow-growing protective oxide layer forms and persists above 900 °C in an oxidative or corrosive atmosphere, rather than cracking or spalling? Earlier work investigated CrFeCoNiX and CrMoTiAlY (Y = Ta, Nb, or W) alloy systems and reported that some compositions developed unstable surface oxides prone to cracking and spallation, while the underlying physical causes remain unresolved. Given the requirement for an environmentally stable, chemically inert barrier and prolonged structural integrity, specify what governs the behaviour and why, a controlled comparison against a defined baseline, the predicted observations, the relevant composition, material-state, exposure, and service boundaries, the prior evidence supporting the hypothesis, and an outcome that would falsify it.

generation.hypothesis: In CrFeCoNiX high-entropy alloys, the persistence of a stable, coherent, slow‐growing protective oxide layer above 900 °C is governed by the selective oxidation of the X element. When X is Si or Al, their oxidation leads to the formation of a continuous, strongly adherent SiO2/Al2O3-rich oxide layer that limits oxygen diffusion and maintains structural integrity. Conversely, when X is Mn, its oxidation produces a less refractory, discontinuous oxide that is prone to cracking and spallation.
generation.material_initial_state: CrFeCoNiX high-entropy alloy in a single- or multiphase metallic solid-solution state.
generation.intervention: Exposure of the alloy to temperatures above 900 °C in an oxidative or corrosive atmosphere.
generation.conditions: Sustained exposure at temperatures above 900 °C in an oxygen-rich or corrosive environment, where thermally activated oxidation processes can occur over extended time periods.
generation.structural_mediator: The nature and integrity of the oxide layer formed by the oxidation of the X element (Si, Mn, or Al) mediate the protective barrier properties at high temperature.
generation.mechanism: Preferential oxidation of Si or Al leads to the formation of a dense, slow-growing oxide (SiO2/Al2O3) that adheres to the substrate and minimizes further oxygen ingress. In contrast, Mn oxidizes to form less refractory and more mobile oxides that fail to develop a continuous layer, resulting in cracking and spallation under thermal stresses.
generation.predicted_outcome: Under high-temperature exposure, alloys with X = Si or Al will develop a uniform, adherent, and slow-growing oxide film that remains intact, whereas alloys with X = Mn will exhibit discontinuous oxide scales prone to cracking and spallation.
generation.baseline: A comparable CrFeCoNi alloy without the reactive X element or with an element that does not promote the formation of a refractory oxide layer serves as a baseline, allowing for the comparison of oxide formation behavior.
generation.boundary: This hypothesis applies to CrFeCoNiX alloys in single- or multiphase states, exposed to oxidative or corrosive environments at temperatures exceeding 900 °C. Its validity may not extend to lower temperatures or substantially different alloy systems.
generation.uncertainty: The role of microstructural variations and potential synergistic interactions among other alloying elements in the formation and adherence of the oxide layer is not fully understood, and may affect the overall protective behavior.

falsification_experiment.design: Fabricate a series of CrFeCoNiX alloys with X = Si, Mn, or Al, along with a control CrFeCoNi alloy lacking X. Expose all samples to a controlled oxidative environment at 950 °C for extended durations. Employ surface and cross-sectional analyses using SEM, TEM, and XRD to characterize the oxide layer morphology, composition, and continuity.
measurements: Oxide layer thickness and uniformity via cross-sectional SEM/TEM
Phase identification of the oxide layer through XRD
Adhesion testing (e.g., scratch tests) to assess scale integrity
Surface crack density and spallation evaluation
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the Mn-containing alloy exhibits oxide scale integrity, uniformity, and adhesion equivalent to that of the Si- or Al-containing alloys – or if the control alloy without X demonstrates similar protective oxide behavior – then the mechanism attributing the protective behavior solely to selective oxidation of Si or Al is falsified.
